chunks: Al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, peace be upon them both, that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said:
The 'aqilah does not bear liability for intentional killing, nor for a confession, nor for a settlement.

key_terms.إِقْرَارًا: a confession or admission by the perpetrator
key_terms.اَلْعَاقِلَةُ: the paternal male kin group that may bear financial liability in specific homicide cases
key_terms.تَضْمَنُ: bears liability or responsibility for compensation

ai.seo_question: When does the 'aqilah bear liability in cases of killing according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning liability in cases of killing. It clarifies that the 'aqilah is not responsible for compensation in cases involving intentional action, confession by the perpetrator, or settlement.
